newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps - Fuel oil up on prompt demand.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps - Fuel oil up on prompt demand.

text.p: Singapore fuel oil swaps rose at midday on Tuesday despite weaker overnight crude values as the market looked to regional demand for support, traders said.
"Fuel oil is firm because there are not additional cargoes coming here from the Middle East and demand is quite strong," one trader said.
June fuel oil swaps were last quoted at $101.75/$102.50 per tonne, up from Monday's $101/$102, brokers said.
But the firmer front month value has not filtered down to the further out months with July quoted at $99.50/$100.25, from $100/101 on Monday.
"The spread is widening," one broker said.
The widening spread was partly attributed to lack of market confidence in the further out months as many feel that the current buying support will not be extended to July.
In the physical market, a local trader had over the past week bought about three 20,000 tonne cargoes with the latest traded at $103.50 per tonne on Monday.
Traders said the purchases by the local trader coincided with the reduction of exports from the Middle East due to the strong domestic demand there for the summer.
As a result, prices are poised to gain strength over the next few days if the buying continues unabated as supplies are limited, they said.
Gas oil slipped slightly at midday with June swaps last quoted at $25.35/$25.45 per barrel, down 20 cents from Thursday, while July was indicated at $25.05/$25.15, down 10 cents.
Traders said the slide was in line with the weaker crude market where July Brent closed down 19 cents to $20.16 per barrel on the International Petroleum Exchange.
June jet fuel/gas oil spread or regrade traded in the negative on Monday for the first time for the prompt month at minus 10 cents, brokers said.
June was last quoted at between minus 30 and minus 10 cents, brokers said.
